children: Wall Street rebounded Thursday after Wednesday’s selloff, which followed the Federal Reserve’s first rate hike since 2023.
The blue-chip Dow
closed +0.6%, the benchmark S&P 500 (
) added +1.1%, and the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite
advanced +1.7%.
From a sector-by-sector vantage point, nine of the 11 segments ended higher, with info tech leading the charge. In reverse, financials suffered the most.

"Today’s market action shows what really goes on in the market. Yesterday’s sell-off was triggered because the market knew that as long as the Fed tightens against supply-driven inflation, the ‘real economy’ gets squeezed. That was, and still is, the biggest risk. Today’s market action happened after two weak days for oil, which eases inflation fears and allows longer-term bond rates to fall,” Seeking Alpha analyst Leo Nelissen of Main Street Alpha stated.
The Federal Open Market Committee increased its benchmark interest rate by 25 basis points on Wednesday, as widely expected, the first rate hike in more than three years.

“I don't see the need to stack additional rate hikes on top of Wednesday's just to prove a point, but the Federal Reserve is going to follow what it deems necessary. These rate hikes should not change an investor's portfolio, as stocks have risen during past interest rate hike regimes,” Bob Edwards of Edwards Asset Management stated.
The U.S. 2-Year Treasury yield
dipped 6 basis points to 4.67%, the U.S. 10-Year Treasury yield
slipped lower by 9 basis points to 4.93%, and the U.S. 30-Year Treasury yield
pushed down by 8 basis points to 5.28%.
As for stocks that were on the move, shares of Moderna
closed +8.4%, while shares of CoreWeave
fell -4.1%.
